auraIntro: Explorer, Large Magellanic Cloud is the largest satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, housing the active Tarantula Nebula.
overview: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) is a satellite galaxy orbiting the Milky Way at a distance of 160,000 light-years in the southern constellations Dorado and Mensa.
formation: Formed roughly 11 billion years ago, its irregular shape is caused by gravitational tidal forces exerted by the Milky Way.
structure: Classified as a Magellanic irregular galaxy spanning 14,000 light-years, containing a central stellar bar and roughly 20 billion stars.
discoveryHistory: Observed since antiquity by Southern Hemisphere indigenous populations; cataloged by Persian astronomer Al Sufi in 964 AD and Ferdinand Magellan in 1519.
observationTips: Prominently visible to the naked eye under dark Southern Hemisphere skies as a bright glowing cosmic cloud.
funFacts: Houses the Tarantula Nebula (30 Doradus), the most energetic starburst region in the entire Local Group.
Hosted Supernova SN 1987A, the closest observed supernova explosion since Kepler's Supernova in 1604.
Gravitationally bound to the Milky Way and expected to merge with our galaxy in roughly 2.4 billion years.

cards.title: Milky Way's Premier Satellite
cards.subtitle: Magellanic Irregular & Tarantula Nebula
cards.body: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) orbits 160,000 light-years from Earth, functioning as an invaluable laboratory for studying stellar evolution.

cards.title: 30 Doradus & SN 1987A
cards.subtitle: Most Active Starbirth Engine in Local Group
cards.body: The Tarantula Nebula in LMC spans 1,000 light-years across. Nearby lies remnant SN 1987A, providing key insights into supernova physics.
bulletPoints: Tarantula Nebula is so bright it would cast shadows if placed at Orion Nebula's distance.
SN 1987A emitted a historical burst of neutrinos detected on Earth.
Connected to Small Magellanic Cloud via the Magellanic Bridge gas stream.
